title: Networking: two hosts on a LAN
description: Two Linux machines share a private network segment 'lan' with no DHCP. Configure static IPv4 addresses and prove they can reach each other.
objectives: Read interface information with 'ip addr' and 'ip link'
Assign static IPv4 addresses and understand /24 subnets
Test connectivity with ping and diagnose failures

tasks.title: Give pc1 the address 10.0.0.1/24
tasks.instructions: Each VM has two network cards: the first is for internet access, the second (usually ens4 or enp0s4) is connected to the 'lan' segment. Assign 10.0.0.1/24 to pc1's lan interface.
hints: List the interfaces with 'ip -br link'. The lan card is the one without an address.
The 'ip addr add' command takes an address in CIDR notation and a 'dev' argument. Don't forget to bring the link up.

tasks.title: Give pc2 the address 10.0.0.2/24
tasks.instructions: Do the same on pc2 with 10.0.0.2/24.

tasks.title: Prove connectivity
tasks.instructions: Make sure pc1 can ping pc2 and the other way around.
hints: If ping fails, check that both links are UP and the addresses are in the same subnet.
